doc: Where a vendored binding and a real file of this repository disagree (fbl-implementation Requirement 12). Each entry is checked by the real-file suite: an unlisted disagreement fails, and so does a listed one that has changed or no longer occurs. Never edit a vendored binding, skip a file or weaken an assertion instead.

divergences.reason: mindmap.fbl's branch relation selects /map/**/node/node, the same entries the node element rule selects. FBL section 5.1 gives an entry to the first matching rule, elements before relations, so the node rule claims every node and no branch is ever read; the nesting is still there as each node's parent. Candidate follow-up for etalii.adp: express branches as the node rule's containment only, or let a relation rule read an entry an element rule also claims.

divergences.reason: The registration keeps positions for two variables on-call.cld does not declare (left from earlier edits of the example), so they name no element of the reading and would be pruned as stale at the next write of the registration. The ids of every declared variable agree since the reading takes DISL's natural ids ('variable:<name>', causal-loop-disl-fbl task 6). Candidate follow-up: drop the two stale positions from the example.

divergences.observed: offset 200: The braces of the body do not balance on this line.
divergences.reason: FBL section 4.7 opens a block only when a statement's last non-whitespace character is '{', so 'model { // trailing a brace is legal' opens none and the matching '}' leaves the braces unbalanced, which makes the body unreadable. Structurizr accepts a comment after the brace, and the module reads this fixture. Candidate follow-up for etalii.adp: let FBL section 4.7 ignore a trailing comment matching the binding's comment expression before looking for '{'.

divergences.observed: Connection: the binding lacks 4 (bothgone, fromnowhere, noends, tonowhere)
divergences.reason: The fixture is one of the timeline module's findings corpus, written to hold dangling connection ends on purpose. The difference is between two bindings: the vendored example reads a connection as an FBL relation, and FBL section 5.4 reads no relation whose end names no element; the module's own binding (timeline.fbl) reads a connection as an element whose from and to are references, so every connection is read and the definition reports the dangling end (timeline-disl-fbl finding B2). Candidate follow-up for etalii.adp: let a relation rule read an entry whose end does not resolve, so a host can report it.
